measured.machine: AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX 16-Core (32 logical cores), 92 GiB RAM, Linux 7.0.0 x86_64, go1.26.0, gcc 13.3.0
measured.method: Three runs of `budgets.sh all`; `measured` is the highest of the three. Startup takes the median of 11 runs. Spread across the three runs: size identical, startup 15/15/15 ms.

binary_size_bytes.why: Measured size plus 10%. Two builds of one tree match byte for byte; the CI runner's checkout and module-cache paths (no -trimpath in the release build) and a newer go1.26 patch move it by well under 1% (-trimpath alone saves 98656 bytes here). A breach means new code or a new dependency added over 4 MB: re-measure and raise it in the same PR only when that growth is intended. Re-measured 2026-11-25 on the CI runner at 56385456 bytes: building 98c0076f (the commit that set the 45361912 measurement) with today's toolchain gives 54868568, so the old figure no longer matched its own tree; the 1.0 trunk added about 1.5 MB since.

startup_help_ms.why: CLI startup has no published threshold, so this is a loose limit: about 16 times the measured median, room for a slow shared CI runner, and still under a 300 ms stall at startup, which it must catch (planted with a sleep in main).

startup_version_ms.why: Same reasoning as startup_help_ms: `version` must not do more work at startup than `--help`.

ci_test_suite_seconds.note: Not a budget and not checked by budgets.sh: the duration of the `Run tests with coverage` step of the last 10 successful `Test & Coverage` runs on main (gh run list --workflow test.yml --branch main --status success, then the jobs API), measured 2026-11-02. Re-read it when CI feels slow.
